data.title: Humane Society of Southern Arizona Opens Client-Choice Pet Pantry, Among First in U.S.
data.description:
Humane Society of Southern Arizona Opens Client-Choice Pet Pantry, Among First in U.S.

Humane Society of Southern Arizona Opens Client-Choice Pet Pantry, Among First in U.S.

PR Newswire

TUCSON, Ariz., Oct. 30, 2026

Dart Mart opens to the public on Nov. 18 from 2 to 4 p.m.

TUCSON, Ariz., Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- The Humane Society of Southern Arizona (HSSA) is opening the first client-choice pet pantry in Tucson, AZ, modeled on best practices from human food pantries. The updated on-site pet pantry venue, "Dart Mart," will officially open to the public on Nov. 18 from 2 to 4 p.m. at HSSA's main campus, 635 W. Roger Rd.

In client-choice "super-market" models, visitors choose their own items instead of receiving a pre-packed bag. The model dates to at least 1993, when New York City's West Side Campaign Against Hunger adopted it, and has spread to food pantries nationwide. It has yet to become common among pet pantries. A Feeding America study by NORC at the University of Chicago found that clients at full-choice pantries reported higher satisfaction, more variety, shorter waits, and less wasted food.

"I've worked in animal welfare a long time, and Dart Mart is one of only a handful like it in the country," said Michelle Dosson, Pacific Regional Director at Best Friends Animal Society and a member of HSSA's Board of Directors. "Food pantries learned decades ago that people know what their households need. Dart Mart at HSSA is the next chapter for dignity in animal welfare services, and I am so proud we are a part of it."

At Dart Mart, each household gets 300 points a month to spend. Every item has a point value, and an attendant helps with checkout. The pantry sees over 2,000 visits a year. The space is styled like a corner market, with colorful storefront windows.

Dart Mart is named for Dart, a beloved German Shepherd mix, by his person, L. Wilson, whose gift gave the space its name. She found him in 2015, when she saw him and his mother in busy traffic.

"I stopped and opened the car door, and both jumped in. It was apparent they were in trouble, hungry, and confused. Of course they came home with me," Wilson said. She took Dart to HSSA to be scanned for a microchip, vaccinated, and neutered. He showed signs of head trauma and managed multiple physical challenges throughout his life.

"Dart had a myriad of quirks which made me love him even more. Quite frankly, Dart was a magnificent dog. He was so loved, and I'm honored to share our love with other families in his memory," Wilson added.

Michele Figueroa, Chief Programs Officer at HSSA, started the Pet Pantry as it is known today when she joined the executive team three years ago. Figueroa has been spearheading the next evolution of this service, which is built on decades of food distribution efforts at the organization.

"People know their pets better than we do," said Figueroa. "If your dog needs a harness, you get to pick your favorite from what's on the shelf. If your cat loves a certain toy, grab it. Same with food: pick the kind your pet loves best. Our clients deserve the dignity of choice."

Dart Mart runs on donated goods. Greater Good Charities provided 90% of the food and supplies on its shelves.

"The Humane Society of Southern Arizona is leading the way in how pet pantries serve their communities," said Liz Baker, CEO of Greater Good Charities. "Dart Mart lets families choose the food and supplies their pets actually need, so every donation goes where it helps most. We're proud to support HSSA's Pet Pantry and to see them show up for Southern Arizona with such empathy and care."

Dart Mart is part of HSSA's Love Stays Home program, which helps families keep their pets rather than surrender them to shelters.

"A pet that stays home is a pet who does not need a kennel," said Dr. Kristin Barney, CEO of HSSA. "This is a success for the pet, the person, and the shelters. Love Stays Home runs on donations, and Dart Mart is a good example of what that support funds."

The pantry joins other efforts at HSSA to keep pets with their families, including last year's collaboration to enhance Pima County's Pet Support Center, funded by a $1.9M grant from Maddie's Fund.

Dart Mart also marks a launch within HSSA's 10,000 Acts of Love campaign. Pet food and supplies are welcome at HSSA, and gifts of any size help keep programs like Dart Mart open. To give, visit hssaz.org/donate. To learn more about Dart Mart, visit hssaz.org/pet-pantry.

About the Humane Society of Southern Arizona
Officially incorporated in 1944, the Humane Society of Southern Arizona is the oldest and largest animal welfare nonprofit in southern Arizona. Its mission is to compassionately serve pets and the people who love them. Learn more at hssaz.org, or visit 635 W. Roger Road, Tucson.

Media Contact: marketing@hssaz.org

data.title: Fitch Lowers France's Outlook to Negative From Stable
data.description:
By Stephen Nakrosis 




  Fitch Ratings said it was lowering its outlook on France's credit rating to negative from Stable, while affirming the country's A+ ratings. 



  The move comes as France faces economic and social pressure over its debt and growing borrowing costs. In recent weeks, hundreds of thousands of people have taken to the streets of Paris and other French cities, with some protesters resorting to vandalism and violence. 



  Fitch said the negative outlook reflects a deterioration since its August review, and cited weaker growth, higher borrowing costs and a wider deficit. These factors are worsening debt dynamics from an already weak starting point, Fitch added. 



  Yields on France's government bonds have also risen since the last review, Fitch said. The agency said it now forecasts interest payments will increase to 3.3% of GDP in 2028 from 2.5% of GDP in 2025. Fitch also sees France's deficit at 5.5% of GDP in 2027, which it said reflects a weaker growth assessment and the risk of concessions during the budget process. 



  The country's A+ rating is supported by a large, wealthy and diversified economy, strong institutions, euro area membership and a resilient banking sector, Fitch added. 



  The next scheduled review date for France's rating hasn't yet been set, Fitch said, but added it expects to review the rating by end-February 2027 at the latest.

Lost Money on O-I Glass, Inc. Shares? The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz Investigates Potential Securities Fraud After 15.01% Stock Decline

Investigation centers on the July 28, 2026 news about O-I Glass, Inc.; investors with losses may have potential claims to recover them

O-I Glass, Inc. ("O-I Glass" or the "Company") investors who lost money may have claims to recover their losses. The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz today announced it is investigating potential securities fraud claims on behalf of investors in O-I Glass, Inc. (NYSE: OI), examining whether the Company may have violated the federal securities laws. The investigation centers on the disclosure about O-I Glass, Inc. on July 28, 2026.

If you lost money on O-I Glass, Inc. securities, share your O-I Glass, Inc. loss information with the firm to learn about potentially pursuing a claim to recover your losses.

O-I Glass, Inc. investigation at a glance

  • Date of disclosure: July 28, 2026
  • Share price decline: $1.36 per share, or 15.01%
  • Closing price: $7.70 on July 29, 2026

What happened?

On July 28, 2026, O-I Glass announced its second quarter 2026 financial results, substantially reducing its 2026 adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow guidance and realigning its 2027 Investor Day financial targets.

On this news, O-I Glass stock fell $1.36 or 15.01%, to close at $7.70 on July 29, 2026.

"O-I Glass, Inc. shares dropped 15.01% after it was disclosed on July 28, 2026 that O-I Glass had substantially reduced its 2026 adjusted EBITDA and free cash flow guidance and realigned its 2027 Investor Day financial targets. Our investigation will look at whether investors had complete and accurate information before that disclosure," said Frank R. Cruz of The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz.

What should O-I Glass, Inc. investors do now?

The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz is investigating potential claims on behalf of O-I Glass, Inc. investors. Investors who lost money can visit the O-I Glass, Inc. investigation page, email info@frankcruzlaw.com, or call 310-914-5007.

If you inquire by email, please include your mailing address, telephone number, and number of shares purchased.

Questions and answers about the O-I Glass, Inc. investigation

Who is eligible? Investors who purchased O-I Glass, Inc. securities and suffered losses may have claims, and can contact the firm to find out whether the O-I Glass, Inc. investigation affects them.

What does a securities fraud investigation involve? In the O-I Glass, Inc. investigation, The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz is examining whether the Company or its executives may have made false or misleading statements to investors in violation of the federal securities laws.

Is there a lawsuit? This release announces an investigation by The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz, not a lawsuit. If a securities class action is later filed against O-I Glass, Inc., investors may be able to seek appointment as lead plaintiff.

How are attorneys' fees handled? The Law Offices of Frank R. Cruz works on contingency, so O-I Glass, Inc. investors pay no attorneys' fees up front. Any attorneys' fees and litigation expenses come only from a recovery, if there is one, and require court approval.

Information for whistleblowers

Anyone with non-public information about O-I Glass, Inc. should consider their options to assist the investigation or participate in the SEC Whistleblower Program. The program allows whistleblowers who provide original information leading to a successful SEC enforcement action to receive awards of 10 to 30 percent of the sanctions collected, when those sanctions exceed $1 million. For more information, contact Frank R. Cruz at 310-914-5007 or email info@frankcruzlaw.com.

data.title: BKFC Founder David Feldman Steps Up for Harassed Michigan Worker with Donation and All-Expenses-Paid Family Cruise Invitation
data.description:
BKFC Founder David Feldman Steps Up for Harassed Michigan Worker with Donation and All-Expenses-Paid Family Cruise Invitation

Feldman invites Red Baron employee Walter Zerod and his family to join BKFSea as special guests, in solidarity against bullying and in support of hardworking Americans

Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship (BKFC) founder and president David Feldman is stepping up in a big way to support Walter Zerod, a Michigan Red Baron employee whose treatment by a streamer sparked national outrage and an outpouring of support. Feldman has pledged a personal donation to the growing fundraising effort and is going one step further, inviting Zerod and his family on an all-expenses-paid Caribbean getaway to BKFSea in January 2027.

BKFSea sets sail aboard Norwegian Jewel, traveling from Miami to Nassau, Bahamas. More than just a vacation, the one-of-a-kind experience will put Zerod and his family in the heart of the BKFC action, with live bare-knuckle fights at sea, exclusive opportunities to meet BKFC stars, nonstop entertainment and unforgettable experiences alongside fighters and fans.

Feldman was moved to act after learning about the worker’s experience through the GoFundMe campaign. According to the fundraiser, a streamer approached the employee and pretended to steal money using his phone, then laughed as the worker explained his distress. The campaign was launched to help provide financial support for the employee and his family amid uncertainty following the incident.

“We’re a combat sports organization, but there’s no place for bullying or humiliating someone who’s just trying to do their job,” said Feldman. “This man was working hard to provide for his family, and somebody decided his dignity was worth sacrificing for a few clicks. That’s wrong, and the moment I saw this, I had to respond. Nobody should have to endure humiliation while trying to earn a living.”

The donation and invitation reflect Feldman’s commitment to turning an act of disrespect into meaningful support. Along with helping to ease the family’s immediate financial pressure, he wants to welcome them into a BKFC community that stands up for people who deserve better.

“Our fans are as tough as they come, and they have big hearts,” Feldman continued. “We stand up for hardworking Americans, like Walter. We want them to enjoy themselves on the cruise, feel welcome and know that the entire BKFC family and community is in their corner.”

BKFSea is the ultimate combat sports cruise, bringing the excitement of Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship (BKFC) to the high seas for an unforgettable, one-of-a-kind fan experience. Taking place January 22–25, 2027, aboard the Norwegian Jewel, the three-night voyage sails from Miami to Nassau, Bahamas, combining live bare-knuckle fighting, exclusive fighter meet-and-greets, interactive fan experiences, live entertainment, nightlife and more. Designed to bring fans closer to the action and their favorite BKFC personalities than ever before, BKFSea delivers an immersive, action-packed getaway that blends world-class combat sports with the excitement of a Caribbean cruise. For more information and reservations, visit www.BKFSea.com⁠

Those wishing to support Walter and his family can visit the GoFundMe campaign.

About Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship

Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship (BKFC) is the first promotion allowed to hold a legal, sanctioned, and regulated bare knuckle event in the United States since 1889. Based in Philadelphia, and headed by President and former professional boxer David Feldman, BKFC is dedicated to preserving the historical legacy of bare knuckle fighting, while utilizing a specifically created rule set that emphasizes fighter safety. BKFC holds all of its bouts in a revolutionary circular four-rope ring, designed to encourage fast-paced and exciting bouts. The patented BKFC “Squared Circle” contains scratch lines, based on the Broughton Rules which governed bare knuckle fighting in the 19th century, and which requires fighters to “Toe the Line”: start every round face to face, and just inches apart.

In BKFC, only those fighters who are established professionals in boxing, MMA, kickboxing, or Muay Thai are allowed to compete. The referees and judges are required to have extensive professional combat sports experience. All fights are held under the auspices and control of an Athletic Commission. Unlike other fighting organizations and combat sports internationally which claim to be “bare knuckle”, but require wraps, tape, and gauze; BKFC is true to its word as fighters are not allowed to wrap their hands to within one inch of the knuckle. This makes BKFC unquestionably the truest form of bare knuckle fighting. BKFC is dedicated to not just creating the safest, most exciting, and highest-level bare-knuckle fighting organization in the world, it’s also leading the way for a new fully recognized professional combat sport. BKFC is truly the sport of the future, which fully respects its remarkable past.

data.title: Adicet Bio Reports Inducement Grant under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4)
data.description:
Adicet Bio Reports Inducement Grant under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4)

Adicet Bio, Inc. (Nasdaq: ACET), a clinical stage biotechnology company discovering and developing allogeneic gamma delta CAR-T cell and in vivo CAR T therapies for autoimmune diseases, hematologic malignancies and solid tumors, today announced it granted an inducement award on October 30, 2026.

One individual was hired by Adicet in October 2026 and granted new hire non-qualified stock options to purchase 1,500 shares of Adicet’s common stock with an exercise price of $3.42 per share, the closing price of Adicet’s common stock as reported by Nasdaq on October 30, 2026. One-fourth of the shares underlying the employee’s option will vest on the one-year anniversary of the employee’s start date and thereafter the remaining three-fourths of the shares underlying the employee’s option will vest in thirty-six substantially equal monthly installments, such that the shares underlying the option granted to the employee will be fully vested on the fourth anniversary of the employee’s start date, subject to the employee’s continued employment with Adicet on such vesting dates.

The above-described award was granted outside of Adicet’s stockholder-approved equity incentive plans pursuant to Adicet’s 2022 Inducement Plan (the Inducement Plan), which was adopted by the board of directors in January 2022 and subsequently amended in January 2023. The award was authorized by the compensation committee of the board of directors, which is comprised solely of independent directors, as a material inducement to the employee entering into employment with Adicet in accordance with Nasdaq Listing Rule 5635(c)(4).

About Adicet Bio, Inc.

Adicet Bio, Inc. is a clinical-stage biotechnology company discovering and developing a broad pipeline of allogeneic gamma delta T cell therapies, engineered with chimeric antigen receptors (CARs), alongside differentiated in vivo CAR-T therapies with the potential to redefine treatment across autoimmune diseases, hematologic malignancies and solid tumors.
